title: The wilderness of the El Paso Mountains
text: The El Paso Mountains Wilderness covers about 23,780 acres and was created in 1994. Its central feature is Black Mountain, an extinct volcano and the highest point in the range. Wildlife there includes raptors, the Mohave ground squirrel, and the desert tortoise. Joshua trees grow on the western side of the mountain.
